-A.Name: -A
-A.description:
Specify the input address base.  The argument base may be
one of d, o, x or n, which specify decimal, octal,
hexadecimal addresses or no address, respectively

-B.Name: -B
-B.description: Output octal shorts.  Equivalent to -t o2

-D.Name: -D
-D.description: Output unsigned decimal ints.  Equivalent to -t u4

-F.Name: -F
-F.description: Output double-precision floating point numbers.  Equivalent to -t fD

-H.Name: -H
-H.description: Output hexadecimal ints.  Equivalent to -t x4

-I.Name: -I
-I.description: Output signed decimal longs.  Equivalent to -t dL

-L.Name: -L
-L.description: Output signed decimal longs.  Equivalent to -t dL

-N.Name: -N
-N.description: Dump at most length bytes of input

-O.Name: -O
-O.description: Output octal ints.  Equivalent to -t o4

-X.Name: -X
-X.description: Output hexadecimal ints.  Equivalent to -t x4

-a.Name: -a
-a.description: Output named characters.  Equivalent to -t a

-b.Name: -b
-b.description: Output octal bytes.  Equivalent to -t o1

-c.Name: -c
-c.description: Output C-style escaped characters.  Equivalent to -t c

-d.Name: -d
-d.description: Output unsigned decimal shorts.  Equivalent to -t u2

-e.Name: -e
-e.description: Output double-precision floating point numbers.  Equivalent to -t fD

-f.Name: -f
-f.description: Output single-precision floating point numbers.  Equivalent to -t fF

-h.Name: -h
-h.description: Output hexadecimal shorts.  Equivalent to -t x2

-i.Name: -i
-i.description: Output signed decimal ints.  Equivalent to -t dI

-j.Name: -j
-j.description:
Skip skip bytes of the combined input before dumping.  The
number may be followed by one of b, k, m or g which
specify the units of the number as blocks (512 bytes),
kilobytes, megabytes and gigabytes, respectively

-l.Name: -l
-l.description: Output signed decimal longs.  Equivalent to -t dL

-o.Name: -o
-o.description: Output octal shorts.  Equivalent to -t o2

-s.Name: -s
-s.description: Output signed decimal shorts.  Equivalent to -t d2

-t.Name: -t
-t.description:
Specify the output format.  The type argument is a string
containing one or more of the following kinds of type specificers: a,
c, [d|o|u|x][C|S|I|L|n], or f[F|D|L|n]. See the man page for meanings

-v.Name: -v
-v.description: Write all input data, instead of replacing lines of duplicate values with a '*'

-x.Name: -x
-x.description: Output hexadecimal shorts.  Equivalent to -t x2
